subject: Non-reactive data - best way to set up a display that depends at different times on different inputs

messages.author: a60d28d0ae3bdda8
messages.subject: Non-reactive data - best way to set up a display that depends at different times on different inputs
parts:
Hi,

I want to set up a display that is based on two sets of inputs -- call them Option A and Option B.

If I update Option A, I want to regenerate both the data and the appearance components of the display.
If I update Option B, I want to only regenerate the appearance component of the display.

If I just make the display reactive to both input options, then the data is regenerated as well as the appearance components of the display, whenever I change Option B.

So far the way I've solved this is by making the data and appearance components into global variables, so that I can persist the data component outside of the reactive Shiny structure, even when the appearance component is reacting to input changes. But this seems a bad way to fix the problem (I was always taught to avoid global variables wherever possible).

I have an idea that might work: separate Options A and B into different input UI panels, tie the data component of the display to a reactive element, and isolate that element so that it only gets updated when the user presses a Submit button on the Option A panel. But I don't know if that would work (I haven't looked into the Isolate feature in detail yet), or whether it would be the best/cleanest way to do it.

If you have any other suggestions for better ways I could achieve this, I'd love to hear them.

Thanks very much

messages.subject: Re: Non-reactive data - best way to set up a display that depends at different times on different inputs
parts:
i think ou can use reactives e.g.

data_for_output <- reactive({
   input$optionA
 ... some code used to generate the data ...
})

output$youroutput <- renderPlot({
  input$optionB
  data <- isolate(data_for_output())
   ....something to generate the output you want...
})

I think you want something like this: optionA now will cause data_for_input() to recompute which in turn will cause output$youroutput to recompute. Chagning optionB doesn't affect data_for_output, but it affects output$youroutput.

messages.subject: Re: Non-reactive data - best way to set up a display that depends at different times on different inputs
parts:
Hi ZJ,

That's really helpful - clarifies things for me.

Unfortunately, after thinking more about the problem, I've realised it's more complicated than I first stated.

The data component of the display only depends on Option A.

The display component depends on Option A and on Option B -- but whenever Option B is updated, I only want to change part of the display component. I want the rest to be perpetuated. If I change Option A, I want the whole of the display component to change.

Basically, I have a list of colours that I want to associate with the different sections of my data. If I choose a new subset of data to display (that's Input A), I want to regenerate the whole set of colours. But I also have a part of the options where the user can change the colour of one section of the data at a time (that's Input B). But I want to perpetuate their choices for the other sections, not regenerate them all.

I guess it might be possible to re-design the input interface so I have conditional input elements, one for every section of the data, that let the user choose the colour for that section of the data.
I know it's possible to have conditional panels, but is it possible to have individual conditional input elements, that are only generated when necessary?

Thanks again

parts:
Currently my supervisor's away, and I'd rather not upload the code without first checking with her, but I've attached a screenshot of the UI.

The reference and include populations are the portions of data selected to view.

Below that is a section allowing the user to choose a particular population, and then alter the colour and shape for plotting that population.

I would like the user to be able to change the colours and shapes for all the populations being plotted. Having separate colour & shape dropdowns for every population selected seemed like too much to fit in the input section. Therefore I thought instead I could set up an interface so they could change the colours and shapes of the different populations one after the other.

Input A is the selection of reference and include populations -- if they change that selection then I want to regenerate a set of colours and shapes for plotting the new selection.
Input B is the selection of a new colour and shape for a single population. If they change that, then I only want to change the colour and shape for that population, but leave previous changes for other populations intact.

As an example, the user might pick the first population, "Mahu", and change its colour to green and its shape to "Triangle", and click Update. The plot points for Mahu will change on the graph. If they then select the "Flat" population and change its colour to purple and its shape to "Square", I still want Mahu to stay plotted as green triangles. I do not want Mahu to be reset to the default generated options, which is black and "Plus".

My simple solution has been to change the vectors of colours and shapes to be global variables, that are perpetuated outside of the reactive data and the functions -- but that's not an ideal solution in the long term.

Is that any clearer? Please tell me if the details are still confusing.

Thanks for your help.
